title: International Trade
overview: Trade analysis explains why specialization creates gains and how restrictions redistribute those gains.
example: Trace a policy or market shock through incentives, quantities, prices, growth, and currency effects.

modules.title: International Trade
modules.explanation: Comparative advantage explains why specialization can raise total output even when one country is more productive in every activity. Tariffs, quotas, and subsidies redistribute gains among consumers, producers, and governments and can provoke retaliation.
steps: Calculate opportunity costs rather than comparing absolute productivity alone.
Identify the efficient specialization and terms-of-trade range.
Trace a trade barrier through price, quantity, surplus, revenue, and deadweight loss.
